messages:
alicia_h: Heads-up — we're rotating a batch of service-account keys next Tue. I realized it will surface as a bunch of 401s for consumers that rely on key_id-based quota/routing. Want to align on fallback and telemetry before the rollout.

meenal_k: Are we still attributing quota to key_id? I thought we moved to service_account_id for billing last quarter.

rick_sre: We attribute billing to service_account_id in billing pipelines, but the runtime routing & rate-limits use key_id today for affinity and fine-grained circuit-breaking. That's why rotation shows up as sudden spikes.

jason_pm: From a console/UX POV we need two things: (1) a visible count of affected tokens + owners, and (2) a recommended migration path that minimizes customer impact. :warning:

alicia_h: Proposal: switch quota attribution to service_account_id for global rate limits, but keep key_id for audit/metrics. Add a short grace window where revoked keys fall through to SA-level quotas for N seconds. Example config: `{"quota_attr":"service_account","legacy_fallthrough_ttl":3600}`

meenal_k: That TTL seems long. 3600s = 1h. I'd prefer 300s for most customers, 3600 only for enterprise migrations. We should make it a per-tenant flag.

rick_sre: Agreed. Operational concerns: fallthrough creates cache churn on the edge — we need to ensure our per-route token cache keys include service_account_id when enabled, otherwise we'll blow up memory with mixed keys. Also need to rate-limit the exchange attempts to avoid thundering herd.

alicia_h: Good call. Implementation sketch:
```
auth.routing.key = lookup(key_id) -> {status, service_account_id}
if status == revoked and allow_legacy_fallthrough then
  attribute = service_account_id
  apply_quota_with_backoff()
else
  reject 401
end
```
Keep audit logs keyed by key_id.

jason_pm: For console: add a dashboard tile showing "active fallthroughs" and a per-SA list with owners + contact. Also an opt-in toggle per org for "allow legacy fallthrough" with default = off.

meenal_k: Telemetry: we should emit these events: `fallthrough.start`, `fallthrough.succeeded`, `fallthrough.rate_limited`, `fallthrough.expired`. Also tag with `route`, `model`, `sa_id`, and anonymized key hash. That helps surface problematic clients.

auth-bot: deploy-bot: auth-service v2.3.0 will include "legacy fallthrough" behind feature-flag. Canary plan: enable for 5% of traffic in staging tomorrow, 0.5% in prod for first 24h.

rick_sre: Add circuit-breaker: if fallthrough.succeeded rate drops below 50% for a given SA over 10m, auto-disable fallthrough for that SA and generate paging alert.

alicia_h: Next steps: (1) meenal + rick to draft config + runtime changes PR, (2) jason to spec console banner + dashboard tile, (3) ops-bot to run canary and collect fallthrough metrics, (4) we set default TTLs: 300s for self-serve orgs, 3600s for enterprise on request. I'll own the rollout doc.

jason_pm: I'll also add copy for the banner: "We're rotating keys — enable legacy fallthrough to reduce immediate failures. This is temporary and will be audited." :memo:

alicia_h: Thanks — syncing up 1:1 after stand to confirm timelines.

rick_sre: I'll add the cache-change PR to the runbook so on-call knows memory impact.

meenal_k: I'll open the telemetry events PR and include example Grafana queries.

auth-bot: deploy-bot: canary toggles scheduled: staging 05:00 UTC, prod rollout gate at 24h metrics check.
